# The Country Club AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition


**by Mike Waldron**


## Why This Report Exists


Country clubs operate under a different kind of financial scrutiny than most businesses. Every dollar that moves through F&B, the pro shop, or the maintenance shed eventually shows up in a board meeting, and a Controller who can’t explain a variance is having a very different conversation than one who can. Member-governed doesn’t mean less pressure. It often means more.


A Baldor invoice with a mispriced case of produce, or a Department Head coding to whatever GL code feels right that month, isn’t just a bookkeeping inconvenience. It’s a number the Finance Committee will eventually ask about.


Most Controllers know something is off long before they can prove it. They know COGS looks high this month, but pinning down whether that’s price creep from a broadliner or a coding error takes hours they don’t have. That gap, between sensing a problem and documenting it, is where club AP has always struggled.


We process hundreds of thousands of invoices for our country club customers. This report is what that data actually shows, not industry estimates, not survey responses, but numbers pulled from real club operations.


This is the first edition. Twice a year, we’ll track how these numbers move, flag what’s driving the changes, and give clubs a benchmark they can actually use. This edition covers duplicate detection, fraud exposure, invoice discrepancies, payment errors, invoice lifecycle time, and AP labor savings.


## Profitability Benchmarks


### Duplicate Detection


**Benchmark** : Country club customers saved $161.4 million on 126,721 duplicate invoices flagged and prevented.


In summer 2026, Ottimate flagged 75,794 duplicate invoices, saving customers $98 million in overspending. That’s already past 50 percent of the prior year’s total, with two quarters still to go.


Duplicate invoices are common wherever F&B volume is high, and approval routing has multiple stops: the Department Head codes, the Controller reviews, and the GM signs off. Somewhere in that chain, the same invoice gets submitted twice. As duplicates trend upward, automated flagging stops being a nice-to-have and becomes the only reliable backstop.


### Fraud Risk


**Benchmark** : 72.3 percent of country club clients had at least one invoice flagged for overcharges or fraud, totaling $47.4 million in exposure.


In the first half of 2026, 66 percent of country club accounts had a flagged invoice, averaging $4,531 an invoice in exposure.


Continuous monitoring clearly contains active risk relative to the full-year benchmark. But with 66 percent of country clubs having a flagged invoice in just six months is a reminder that the threat hasn’t gone away. It’s being caught before it becomes a loss, which is a different thing from not existing.


### Credit Recovery


**Benchmark:** Ottimate uncovered $144.3 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments, and overcharge corrections last year.


In the first half of 2026, Ottimate uncovered $132.1 million in credits related to refunds, adjustments and overcharges for country clubs alone.


With continuous pricing increases, and invoice volumes on the rise, we continue to see the amount of overcharges increase. Implementing automation into your workflow is more important than ever to make sure you are catching these costly mistakes before they hit your bottom line.


## Payments


**Benchmark** : Ottimate caught 14,250 payments with errors last year, accounting for $1.6 million in potential losses.


So far this year, Ottimate has caught 6,026 payments with errors, accounting for $1.01 million in potential losses.


Payment errors are costly and difficult to recover from once funds have left the account. Clubs are already closing in on last year’s full total halfway through this one. Manual payment reviews miss what automated checks consistently catch, making a final validation layer before disbursement a critical control, not an optional one.


# Productivity Benchmarks


## Invoice Lifecycle Time


**Benchmark** : Country club customers using Ottimate have reduced invoice lifecycle time from upload to approval from 11 days down to 7.2 days on average.


In the first half of 2026, country club customers dropped to 4.0 days on average, the best result we’ve tracked.


This is roughly half the established benchmark. For a club running a multi-step approval chain, Department Head to Controller to GM, that kind of speed doesn’t happen by accident. It reflects deeper platform adoption and approval workflows that have been built out, not bolted on.


## AP Labor Savings


**Benchmark** : Ottimate saves country clubs $40,500 per account per year in labor by reducing invoice lifecycle time.


Country club accounts are now saving an average of 7.0 days per invoice, up from the 6.4-day benchmark.


The original labor savings benchmark now looks conservative. As lifecycle time keeps dropping, the time Controllers and AP staff get back, time that used to go toward chasing approvals and reconciling F&B invoices, keeps growing.


## About This Report


The Country Clubs AP Automation Benchmark Report: Summer 2026 Edition is published by Ottimate using aggregated, anonymized data from our grocery customer base. All benchmarks reflect real invoice processing data across independent and regional grocery operators. This is the first edition; future editions will track trends and flag what’s driving the changes.
